items.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 18 at 1:20PM PST until November 18 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
items.description:
* WHAT...South winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 55 mph expected.

* WHERE...San Francisco and San Francisco Bay Shoreline, The Central
Coast, The Santa Clara Valley and Eastern Hills, and The Santa Cruz
Mountains.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM PST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Wind gusts up to 70 mph will be possible in
the higher terrain.
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

items.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 18 at 1:05PM PST until November 18 at 3:30PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
items.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Coastal San Francisco Peninsula

* WHEN...Until 330 PM PST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways. Ponding of water in urban or other areas is
occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 105 PM PST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. This  will
cause urban and small stream flooding. Between 0.5 and 0.75
inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.5 inches are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
San Francisco, Daly City, Pacifica, Half Moon Bay, El Granada,
Moss Beach, Montara and Broadmoor.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
items.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

items.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 18 at 8:08AM PST until November 18 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, an increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 12
to 17 ft. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.2 ft of
inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves of 18 to 24 ft with up to 30 ft at favored
breakpoints along the coast from this afternoon through Friday
morning.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 AM PST Friday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 4 PM PST this
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM this
afternoon to 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without
warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM
Thursday and 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45 AM Friday.
These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will
enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide
varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast
and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
items.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

items.headline: Gale Warning issued November 18 at 8:38AM PST until November 18 at 3:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
items.description:
* WHAT...South winds 25 to 35 kt with gusts up to 45 kt and seas
8 to 13 ft.

* WHERE...Coastal Waters from Point Reyes to Pigeon Point
California out to 10 NM.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM PST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
items.instruction:
Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.
Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for severe conditions.
